page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processors. Featuring 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading operating at a 4.5 GHz base frequency, this x86_64 architecture node offers direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. System memory is provisioned with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The server does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage architectures supported by a 100 Gbps network interface.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive memory and compute throughput. Memory evaluations place the node in the top tier (top 10%) on the PassMark memory score (3005.24), backed by strong uncached 256 MB read bandwidth of 235.79 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 97.89 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks show solid results, including a strong PassMark CPU score of 50205.16 and high software compilation performance on Geekbench (40579.0). Single-core and multi-core evaluations via stress-ng (1881.29 and 58900.54) and Geekbench (1588.0 single-core, 13741.0 multi-core) register in the middle 50% category.

Instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), AES cryptography, and hardware-assisted virtualization (VMX). While prompt processing for small and medium language models remains average, LLM text generation is constrained, registering poor to weak performance (41.36 tokens/sec on 135M models and 7.88 tokens/sec on 7B models) due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. With its high clock speed, large memory bandwidth, and 100 Gbps networking, the instance is well suited for code compilation, CI/CD pipelines, in-memory databases, and high-frequency network-bound enterprise workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server delivering dedicated access to a 48-vCPU (24 physical cores) Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at 4.5 GHz. Equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, it features no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. The server achieves top-tier memory marks on PassMark alongside strong uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth. Compute testing displays solid software compilation scores and strong overall PassMark CPU performance, while single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place within median levels. Due to the lack of hardware accelerators, LLM generation performance is limited, but high per-core clock rates and high-bandwidth networking make it a reliable platform for software builds, CI/CD build nodes, containerized environments, and network-intensive enterprise workloads.
